title: HARD HEARTS THAT REFUSE TO COME

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. But they said, "We will not come! Isn't it enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? And now you also want to lord it over us! Moreover, you haven't brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Do you want to treat these men like slaves? No, we will not come!" — Num 16:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses reaches out even to Dathan and Abiram, summoning them — an invitation to talk, perhaps even a door to reconciliation. But their answer is a flat, hardened refusal: "We will not come!" Twice they say it. Their hearts are shut, and they will not even come to the table.

Look at how twisted their words have become. They call Egypt — the land of their slavery — "a land flowing with milk and honey," a phrase that rightly belonged to the Promised Land. Bitterness has rewritten their memory. The place of chains now looks golden, and the God who rescued them is cast as the villain. When our hearts turn hard, we start telling ourselves stories where we are the wronged ones and God is against us.

Notice too their accusation that they had not been brought into the good land "or given an inheritance." But whose fault was that? It was the people's own unbelief in refusing to enter, as we read two chapters ago. They blame Moses for a delay their own rebellion had caused. A hardened heart never takes responsibility; it always finds someone else to blame.

This is a sobering picture of what unrepented bitterness does. It refuses the invitation, rewrites the past, and blames everyone but itself. And yet how patient God is, still reaching out through Moses even now. The gospel is the greatest invitation of all — God in Christ calling rebels to come home. The tragedy is not that the door is closed, but that hard hearts refuse to walk through it. May we never say to God, "We will not come," but always answer His call with a yielded heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there any area where your heart has grown hard and refuses to come to God?
2. How does bitterness rewrite our memories and shift the blame?
3. How will you respond to God's patient invitation to come to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep my heart soft and never let bitterness harden me against You. Forgive me when I blame others for what my own choices have caused. Help me always to answer Your gracious invitation with a willing "yes." Amen.
